prd.note: Initial Pulse integrations requirement set; proposed, not yet approved.

rows.covers: Connect-once access to authorized work context across Pulse Code clients and environments.
rows.action: Confirm outcome language and connection ownership assumptions.
rows.live: User request plus existing settings/source-control architecture.

rows.covers: Provider capability groups, prioritization criteria, and the system-of-record boundary.
rows.action: Define tokenizer and collect provider-demand evidence before promoting candidates.
rows.live: Pulse Issues in-flight work and existing multi-host source-control adapters.

rows.covers: Connect, reauthorize, map, health, native context, action preview, and disconnect UX.
rows.action: Resolve user-owned versus environment-admin-owned connection scenarios.
rows.live: /settings/integrations exists; Pulse Issues connection UI is in flight.

rows.covers: Server ownership, durable records, thin adapters, bounded reads, optional capabilities, and receipts.
rows.action: Execute T1 and use a second-adapter spike to test the abstraction.
rows.live: Typed RPC/capability patterns exist; shared integration contracts are planned.

rows.covers: Credential isolation, least privilege, OAuth/webhook protection, remote clients, and mixed versions.
rows.action: Complete T2 secret-store/OAuth review before storing refresh tokens.
rows.live: Current server secret store and Issues PAT boundary are evidence; OAuth guarantees are unverified.

rows.covers: Connect/fix/recovery/compatibility metrics and adapter-by-adapter rollout gates.
rows.action: Measure the reference adapter before setting numeric targets.
rows.live: Metric names exist; baselines and targets remain explicit nulls in the roadmap.

rows.covers: Testable connection, context/action, multi-surface, remote, safety, migration, and second-adapter proof.
rows.action: Review and approve before implementation begins.
rows.live: Mapped to the ten-task implementation DAG; no implementation receipts yet.

rows.covers: Separates official T3 authority from the downstream Pulse desktop product.
rows.action: Keep release and implementation changes inside the locked product boundary.
rows.live: Pulse desktop identity work and focused package receipts are recorded in the roadmap.

rows.covers: Defines upstream intake, downstream ownership, and Pulse-only divergence.
rows.action: Continue explicit reviewable upstream intake without claiming parity.
rows.live: The repository has separate origin and upstream remotes; Pulse artifacts are downstream-owned.

rows.covers: Requires isolated desktop identity, state, protocols, packaging, and update ownership.
rows.action: Finish platform lifecycle proof before team-wide release.
rows.live: Pulse-specific IDs, paths, schemes, and package identities are implemented with focused tests.

rows.covers: Requires fresh Pulse state and explicit nondestructive future import.
rows.action: Keep automatic T3 discovery or migration out of first run.
rows.live: Pulse owns a separate desktop state root; no import workflow is claimed.

rows.covers: Keeps web and mobile shared and capability-aware initially.
rows.action: Preserve shared clients until a separate locked product decision exists.
rows.live: Web remains shared with desktop and mobile uses the common capability model.

rows.covers: Bounds the work to permanent Pulse desktop distribution and side-by-side operation.
rows.action: Complete remaining install and lifecycle evidence on every desktop platform.
rows.live: Identity implementation and Windows candidate inspection are recorded; full platform proof remains open.

rows.covers: Excludes T3 publishing, automatic sync or migration, and separate web/mobile identities.
rows.action: Reject changes that cross these boundaries without a new decision.
rows.live: No live implementation is claimed for excluded work.

rows.covers: Requires package inspection and side-by-side proof on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
rows.action: Collect macOS, Linux, and complete lifecycle receipts before release.
rows.live: Windows package inspection exists; the roadmap explicitly leaves cross-platform release evidence open.

rows.covers: Connects the requirement to acceptance, decisions, gaps, and upstream authority.
rows.action: Keep linked authorities synchronized when the boundary changes.
rows.live: Acceptance criteria, decisions, gaps, and upstream remote are present.

rows.covers: Tracks import categories and permanent per-platform identities still to settle.
rows.action: Close identity questions before release and import questions before shaping import.
rows.live: Some Pulse identities are implemented; import remains unimplemented and unshaped.

rows.covers: Defines unreliable mobile file-link activation and the missing native fallback.
rows.action: Retain visible fallback behavior for recognized workspace-file links.
rows.live: Mobile file-link actions were approved and implemented with focused evidence.

rows.covers: Provides Preview and remote-safe Open with actions plus honest failure handling.
rows.action: Monitor the shipped behavior and preserve unchanged web/desktop paths.
rows.live: Focused mobile behavior and signed asset routing are implemented and verified.

rows.covers: Excludes progress, persistent downloads, offline queues, new endpoints, and provider changes.
rows.action: Keep durable-download follow-up work separately scoped.
rows.live: Durability was split into PRD 14 instead of expanding this slice.

rows.covers: Requires signed routes across connection modes, workspace containment, and temporary cache storage.
rows.action: Retain focused remote and containment coverage.
rows.live: The existing signed asset route and mobile cache path implement the boundary.

rows.covers: Defines forward update as a one-way door when renderer or server health fails.
rows.action: Keep rollback reachable independently of renderer and backend health.
rows.live: Rollback and Help-menu safe mode are implemented with focused tests.

rows.covers: Specifies version choice, crash-proof access, safety floor, channel integrity, and deliberate install.
rows.action: Collect release-candidate proof and keep floor/channel fixtures green.
rows.live: The working tree implementation and 67 focused tests are recorded in the roadmap.

rows.covers: Excludes database snapshot restore, mobile/CLI rollback, and a second updater mechanism.
rows.action: Shape snapshot/restore separately if schema compatibility demands it.
rows.live: Phase 1 reuses electron-updater and does not claim snapshot restore.

rows.covers: Requires electron-updater reuse, GitHub release source, and a compile-time minimum version.
rows.action: Raise the floor deliberately with incompatible data or identity changes.
rows.live: Feed pinning, rollback floor, and reset behavior are implemented and tested.

rows.covers: Official T3 artifacts remain upstream-owned.
rows.action: Keep Pulse CI from publishing modified T3 artifacts.
rows.live: Origin/upstream repository separation is configured.

rows.covers: Upstream intake is explicit and reviewable.
rows.action: Retain selective pull-request-based intake.
rows.live: A configured upstream remote supports explicit reviewable intake.

rows.covers: Pulse-only features and cadence may diverge without changing T3.
rows.action: Keep divergence within Pulse-owned releases and identities.
rows.live: Pulse-specific product and integration work exists downstream.

rows.covers: Pulse and T3 install without identity or path collisions.
rows.action: Finish side-by-side install proof on every desktop platform.
rows.live: Pulse package identity is implemented; complete cross-platform proof remains open.

rows.covers: Both desktop products can execute simultaneously with separate locks and state.
rows.action: Collect concurrent launch receipts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
rows.live: Distinct application identifiers and state roots are implemented.

rows.covers: Install, update, and uninstall actions cannot mutate the other product.
rows.action: Complete packaged lifecycle tests before release.
rows.live: Pulse updater and package coordinates are distinct; full lifecycle evidence remains open.

rows.covers: Pulse starts from Pulse-owned state without automatic T3 migration.
rows.action: Retain the fresh-state default.
rows.live: Pulse uses its own state root and does not claim automatic import.

rows.covers: Any future import must preview, copy selectively, and leave T3 unchanged.
rows.action: Shape and approve import separately before implementation.
rows.live: No import implementation is claimed.

rows.covers: Web and mobile retain shared product identities and capability-aware behavior.
rows.action: Require a new locked decision before separating either client.
rows.live: Shared web and mobile clients remain in the repository.

rows.covers: Release proof must cover package identity and lifecycle on all desktop platforms.
rows.action: Add macOS, Linux, and complete Windows lifecycle receipts before team rollout.
rows.live: Windows candidate inspection exists; the roadmap does not claim all-platform completion.

rows.covers: Links acceptance to the parent requirement, decisions, gaps, and roadmap.
rows.action: Keep referenced authorities aligned with boundary changes.
rows.live: Parent PRD, decisions, gaps, and roadmap records exist.

rows.covers: Tracks remaining import and permanent identity choices.
rows.action: Resolve release identities before release and import categories before import shaping.
rows.live: Implementation answers part of the identity question; import remains undecided.

rows.covers: Defines the gap between manual coding chats and a bounded unattended daily check-in.
rows.action: Approve the scheduled-chat change request before assigning implementation capacity.
rows.live: No scheduling machinery is claimed; the roadmap keeps this work in Next.

rows.covers: Persistent schedule threads, fresh provider sessions, handoff files, project and environment scopes, and trust rails.
rows.action: Resolve host availability and provider support before promotion to Now.
rows.live: The design and roadmap item exist; no implementation receipt exists.

rows.covers: Excludes a generic workflow engine, canned prompts, silent mutation, and broad notification work.
rows.action: Keep any collaboration notification work in its separate roadmap item.
rows.live: No excluded behavior is claimed.

rows.covers: Requires exactly-once decisions, time leashes, explicit provider support, visible failure, and reviewable diffs.
rows.action: Prove host availability, idempotency, and interruption behavior before release shaping.
rows.live: The host-availability limitation remains documented; deterministic execution is unimplemented.

rows.covers: Runs PulseFlow's full Impeccable design loop in the current coding context without copying document ownership into Pulse Code.
rows.action: Approve the host boundary and cross-repository release train before implementation.
rows.live: Preview host primitives exist, but PulseFlow is specification-only and no integrated session exists.

rows.covers: Inventories reusable Preview tabs, environment routing, capture, automation, and skill-picker primitives.
rows.action: Preserve these behaviors in the local host proof and focused regression suite.
rows.live: The named Preview, broker, capture, and picker surfaces exist in the repository.

rows.covers: Bounds host work to web and desktop Preview, typed tools, routing, reconnect, evidence, and capability skew.
rows.action: Keep model behavior and document mutation in PulseFlow and mobile authoring out of the first release.
rows.live: No PulseFlow-specific host implementation is claimed.

rows.covers: Defines skill discovery, Preview binding, picker events, progressive variants, full iteration controls, accept, discard, and recovery.
rows.action: Build the deterministic local fixture and prove every named control before remote expansion.
rows.live: Existing Preview controls are live; live-design controls and adapter handshake are planned.

rows.covers: Defines an optional versioned capability, bound request identity, runtime validation, and narrow agent tools.
rows.action: Implement contracts and mixed-version fixtures before exposing client controls.
rows.live: The repository has additive capability patterns; this contract does not exist yet.

rows.covers: Assigns browser and transport state to Pulse Code and picker, variant, and transaction authority to PulseFlow.
rows.action: Obtain PulseFlow and Pulse Code owner sign-off before implementation.
rows.live: The proposed boundary is aligned across both repository change requests but remains unsigned.

rows.covers: Defines direct, private-network, public gateway, web-host, mobile, origin, nonce, replay, and session constraints.
rows.action: Design and threat-model the authenticated public Preview gateway.
rows.live: Local and private target resolution exists; public remote resolution is explicitly blocked.

rows.covers: Keeps ordinary Preview available through capability skew, adapter mismatch, disconnect, denial, and bounded evidence failures.
rows.action: Attach mixed-version, redaction, reconnect, and uncertain-outcome receipts to the release review.
rows.live: Existing optional-capability behavior is reusable; live-design failure handling is unimplemented.

rows.covers: Sequences local proof, full interaction, agent and skill, private routing, gateway, and integrated release gates with a 6 to 9 engineering-week estimate.
rows.action: Start only after a real PulseFlow adapter fixture exists and roadmap capacity is assigned.
rows.live: The feasibility judgment is evidence-backed, but implementation and public transport gates remain open.

rows.covers: Links the host PRD to acceptance, sitemap, workflow, tool flow, existing modules, and PulseFlow authority.
rows.action: Keep both repository change requests synchronized when the protocol changes.
rows.live: All local links resolve; the PulseFlow reference is intentionally cross-repository.

rows.covers: Tracks gateway shape, generic source acceptance, and first-release web scope.
rows.action: Resolve during the corresponding rollout slice without weakening the fixed security outcomes.
rows.live: The questions do not block the local deterministic host proof.

rows.covers: Older and newer clients and servers retain ordinary Preview and expose live design only when compatible.
rows.action: Add contracts and mixed-version fixtures.
rows.live: No live-design capability exists yet.

rows.covers: Binds protocol, origin, nonce, environment, thread, tab, document, actor, permission, and operation identity.
rows.action: Test valid, stale, replayed, foreign-origin, and oversized messages.
rows.live: The page adapter and handshake are unimplemented.

rows.covers: Prevents cross-tab and cross-environment event delivery and invalidates stale bindings.
rows.action: Add multi-environment and multi-tab broker fixtures.
rows.live: Existing Preview tabs provide the host identity; live session binding is planned.

rows.covers: Gates every picker, context, variant, tuning, steering, text, acceptance, discard, stop, progress, and recovery control.
rows.action: Run the keyboard and pointer journey against a deterministic PulseFlow fixture.
rows.live: The full interaction set is specified but unimplemented.

rows.covers: Protects viewport, appearance, refresh, screenshot, recording, annotation, and pop-out behavior.
rows.action: Keep the focused Preview regression suite release-blocking.
rows.live: The protected Preview behaviors exist today.

rows.covers: Keeps the root Impeccable skill and all 23 commands discoverable without a partial local metadata copy.
rows.action: Pin upstream metadata and add provider discovery and composer picker fixtures.
rows.live: A composer skill picker exists; the pinned Impeccable integration is planned.

rows.covers: Requires direct user acceptance, exact session and variant identity, idempotency, and authoritative PulseFlow receipts.
rows.action: Test double-click, reconnect, timeout, denial, and stale revision paths.
rows.live: No PulseFlow transaction path exists in Pulse Code.

rows.covers: Prevents duplicate Accept or Discard after transport uncertainty.
rows.action: Add boundary fault injection and idempotency reconciliation fixtures.
rows.live: The proposed broker owns this behavior; it is unimplemented.

rows.covers: Routes environment-port targets to the correct local or private environment without changing another session.
rows.action: Extend resolver fixtures and run real local and private host checks.
rows.live: The underlying environment-host substitution exists.

rows.covers: Requires an authenticated exact-target gateway for public or relay-only environments and rejects raw-port exposure.
rows.action: Implement and security-review the gateway before public remote support.
rows.live: The current resolver explicitly reports this gateway as missing.

rows.covers: Makes page and host focus deterministic across pointer, keyboard, screen reader, Escape, and 200 percent zoom.
rows.action: Add the browser focus matrix and accessibility scan.
rows.live: Existing Preview focus behavior is the baseline; live controls are planned.

rows.covers: Applies schemas, limits, origin checks, and redaction before page data reaches state, logs, prompts, or receipts.
rows.action: Add property-based contracts, secret canaries, and oversized payload fixtures.
rows.live: Existing evidence caps are reusable; the live-design boundary is unimplemented.

rows.covers: Limits mobile to read-only status and handoff when it lacks pointer and Preview host capability.
rows.action: Add capability-skew UI tests and avoid rendering inactive authoring controls.
rows.live: Mobile shares capability patterns but has no live-design status surface.

rows.covers: Gates the real nested target, progressive variants, tune or steer, accept, undo, repeat, discard, and clean teardown journey.
rows.action: Run only after the PulseFlow adapter exists and the upstream Windows baseline is green or explicitly constrained.
rows.live: PulseFlow is specification-only, so no end-to-end product can run today.

rows.covers: Records that gateway shape remains an implementation choice while its required security outcome is fixed.
rows.action: Choose the gateway mechanism during implementation review.
rows.live: No unresolved acceptance outcome remains.

rows.covers: Maps the complete pinned live chrome, copy workflow, controls, errors, protocol lifecycle, and isolation boundary between the Preview host and PulseFlow page.
rows.action: Keep the cross-repository registry fixture release-blocking as upstream evolves.
rows.live: The underlying Preview host exists; the joint live-surface contract is unimplemented.

rows.covers: Gates page-scoped copy Save, Cancel, Apply, discard, repair, rollback, idempotency, and authority boundaries.
rows.action: Add browser and broker fault fixtures after the PulseFlow document adapter exists.
rows.live: The host relay and PulseFlow copy transaction path are unimplemented.

rows.covers: Fails intake when a pinned command, UI surface, action, event, phase, or parameter kind lacks an explicit host mapping.
rows.action: Implement the exact cross-repository registry snapshot test before dependency intake.
rows.live: The audited upstream registries are pinned in the proposal; no automated parity test exists.

roadmap.note: Four shaped Now outcomes, four concept-stage Next candidates, and three Later discoveries; capacity is an assumption pending confirmation.

tasks.note: Ten durable starting tasks; T1 contracts and T2 secret review form the first parallel frontier.
